question: is d_surface a DISTINCT channel from refusal, as §18 claims?
VERDICT: SUPERSEDED by CORRECTION_2026_08_22_audit9 -- see that field.
reading: 'd_surface is a distinct second channel' is NOT supported -- 90% of its effect is inside the refusal effect. 'The two interact' IS supported -- removing both unlocks flips neither unlocks alone. The report's §18 conflates these.
caveat: Containment does not by itself prove d_surface acts THROUGH refusal; both arms may simply recruit the most fragile prompts, the same alternative raised in R-23 for the angle controls. What it does rule out is the claim that d_surface's behavioural effect is largely separate.

CORRECTION_2026_08_22_audit9.F1_interaction_withdrawn: '40 flips neither arm produces alone' is what NO interaction predicts. (B∪C)\D = 1 of 104, so D's flip set is a near-perfect SUPERSET of B∪C; pure monotone nesting under a larger perturbation predicts |D|-|B∪C| = 39 novel flips and 40 were observed. Net interaction evidence: ONE prompt. D is also unambiguously a larger perturbation (91.5% of generations changed vs B 38.2%, C 88.9%). And the 40 is not independent corroboration of §14-SA -- it is the same arithmetic (|D|-|B|-|C| = 20 = 40-19-1).
CORRECTION_2026_08_22_audit9.F2_containment_p_corrected: The published hypergeometric null (uniform over 463 baseline-refusing prompts, E=4.63, p=1.1e-11) is wrong: only ~143/463 prompts are flippable by ANY perturbation. Conditional on D's flip pool: N=143, K=101, n=21, E[overlap]=14.83, observed 19, p=0.0224. Generic flippability alone predicts ~15 of the 19.
CORRECTION_2026_08_22_audit9.revised_verdict: 'Distinct second channel' remains UNSUPPORTED (19/21 = 90.5% contained; the descriptive fact is unchanged), but the evidence is p~0.02 against a fragility-aware null, not 1e-11. 'The two interact' is NOT supported and NOT refuted -- CANNOT DETERMINE, because this design has no dose-matched two-direction comparator.
